content.comment_body: Dear [product_name] community, I'm dealing with old hardware and a persistent issue I couldn't resolve despite searching this forum. Here's my setup: - [article_no] connected via USB cable ([article_no]) to a PC running Windows XP/SP3 (Dell Optiplex 260) - USB to UART Bridge (CP210x) assigned to COM 4 - [product_name] software [version_no] - Another data acquisition device attached to the physical COM1 port - The PC is remotely operated (TeamViewer), which makes troubleshooting difficult What works: - Downloading programs from the device to PC - Setting time and date on the device - Starting and stopping the device Issue: - Attempting to upload a program (even small ones) fails. Common errors are "invalid XOR checksum," and after several tries, only part of the transfer completes before a "timeout," usually around 50%. Troubleshooting already attempted: - Changed COM ports (between 3 and 4) - Modified baud rate and FIFO settings - Power cycled device and PC - Disabled data acquisition device - Reinstalled UART bridge I'm running out of ideas—any suggestions are appreciated! Thanks in advance, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], Have you considered upgrading to the latest version of [product_name] software? If you have an older version already, the upgrade is free. See the demo software, upgrades/updates, and drivers at [url]. Be sure to select the correct version for your operating system. These FAQs guide you through manual and automatic upgrades: - [document] - [document] Although the example covers upgrading to version [version_no], the procedure is identical for [version_no]. With [version_no], your current hardware ([article_no]) should still be supported. Hopefully, updating will resolve your upload/download issues. If not, let us know. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi, Upgrading to [version_no] didn't resolve the issue. The new version checks communication and reports it as OK, but the same problems remain when uploading. I'm attaching screenshots in case they help with further analysis. Thanks for your support! [user_name]
Hi. Just one thought: do you have any memory modules attached to the base unit?

Hi, No memory module is present. I've updated the USB-UART driver, still no result. The program loads at home on the same [product_name] type. The last remote possibility is changing USB ports—any other suggestions? If not, I’ll consider traveling to the site. Thank you for your help, [user_name]

Hi. Sorry to hear about your issue. The [product_name] user community doesn't seem to have a solution. Have you contacted [company_name] support? [url] As a last thought—some users have had problems using USB3 ports. That's all I can suggest.

Hi, Are you able to up/download when directly connected to the [product_name]? If so, then perhaps some intermediate equipment is interfering with communication between the software and the device. It sounds like your setup has multiple connections in the chain. Hope this helps.

Dear [product_name] users, I managed to solve the issue on site within a minute after three hours of travel. The problem was caused by an oxidized contact pin in the device's COM socket. A quick application of contact lubricant restored proper communication. Thanks again for everyone's input! Never forget the two key tools: power tape and penetrating oil spray!

analysis.insight_summary: The user struggled with repeated failures uploading programs from [product_name] software to a [product_name] device via USB, despite successful downloads and basic commands. The problem persisted even after software and driver updates, with errors indicating communication issues. Extensive troubleshooting didn't resolve it until an onsite inspection revealed a physical connection fault—a corroded contact pin. The experience highlights the importance of considering both software and hardware factors in communication problems.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wanted dependable two-way program transfer (uploading and downloading) between [product_name] software and the device, even when using a virtual COM port and USB bridge. They expected that updating software or drivers would address any issues encountered.
